title: ANALYZE, Statistics and PRAGMA optimize
learningObjectives: Explain why query planners use table and index statistics.
Use ANALYZE to gather SQLite statistics.
Inspect sqlite_stat1 entries for a table and index.
Describe the role of PRAGMA optimize in SQLite maintenance.
Re-check query plans and workload performance after significant data changes.

understand.concept: Query planners use statistics to estimate how many rows match a condition and choose an access strategy. SQLite's ANALYZE command gathers statistics; PRAGMA optimize can run targeted analysis work when appropriate.
understand.whyItMatters: Accurate statistics help the optimizer choose better plans as tables grow and data distributions change.
understand.analogy: An index is like a sorted lookup guide that points toward the relevant records instead of requiring every page to be read.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not model B-tree pages, query planner estimates, index maintenance or the full range of SQL access paths.

explain.narrative:
## Why statistics matter
The query planner estimates the cost of candidate strategies. Statistics about table and index contents can improve those estimates, especially when data is unevenly distributed.

## ANALYZE
ANALYZE gathers statistics for tables and indexes and stores them in SQLite's statistics tables, such as sqlite_stat1. Running ANALYZE after significant data changes can help the planner make better choices.

## PRAGMA optimize
PRAGMA optimize is a recommended maintenance entry point in modern SQLite. It may decide that targeted analysis is useful. Its exact work depends on database history and version, so do not assume it always changes statistics.

## Operational caution
Statistics maintenance is not a substitute for inspecting slow queries. Re-check query plans and measure representative workloads after significant schema or data changes.

examples.title: Create a table for planner statistics
examples.code: CREATE TABLE perf15_stats (record_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, category TEXT NOT NULL, amount INTEGER NOT NULL);
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create a table for planner statistics in SQLite. Verify both the access strategy and the returned data.

examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create an index for category lookups in SQLite. Verify both the access strategy and the returned data.

examples.title: Gather table and index statistics
examples.code: ANALYZE perf15_stats; SELECT tbl, idx FROM sqlite_stat1 WHERE tbl = 'perf15_stats' ORDER BY idx;
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates gather table and index statistics in SQLite. Verify both the access strategy and the returned data.

examples.title: Run SQLite's optimization maintenance entry point
examples.code: PRAGMA optimize; SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_rows FROM perf15_stats;
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates run sqlite's optimization maintenance entry point in SQLite. Verify both the access strategy and the returned data.

practise.guidedTask: Run ANALYZE, inspect the statistics row and execute PRAGMA optimize. Explain why statistics can influence plan selection.
practise.independentTask: Create a table with uneven category distribution, add an index, gather statistics and inspect query plans before and after ANALYZE. Record what changed in your SQLite runtime.

questions.prompt: Why do query planners use statistics?
options: To estimate row counts and compare execution strategies

options: Gathers statistics about tables and indexes

questions.prompt: Where are common SQLite planner statistics stored?

A command to disable query planning
